stories.title: Hansel and Gretel
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.place: Kassel, Hesse — told by Dortchen Wild
stories.teaser: During a severe famine, a woodcutter and his wife abandon their two children, Hansel and Gretel, in the deep forest.

stories.title: Little Red-Cap (Little Red Riding Hood)
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: A young girl named Little Red-Cap is sent by her mother to deliver wine and cake to her sick grandmother in the woods, with strict instructions to stay on the main path.

stories.title: Rapunzel
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: A pregnant woman craves rampion from the walled garden of the sorceress Dame Gothel, driving her husband to trespass and barter away their unborn child in exchange for the herb.

stories.title: Rumpelstiltskin
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: A poor miller seeking status falsely brags to the king that his daughter can spin ordinary straw into pure gold, prompting the monarch to lock her in a room under penalty of death.

stories.title: Ashputtel (Cinderella)
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: Following her mother's death, Ashputtel is forced by her cruel stepmother and two haughty stepsisters to sleep in the fireplace cinders and perform domestic drudgery.

stories.title: Snowdrop (Snow White)
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: Envious of Snowdrop's surpassing beauty, an evil queen orders a huntsman to kill her stepdaughter, but he spares the girl, who finds refuge keeping house for seven dwarfs in the mountains.

stories.title: Briar Rose (Sleeping Beauty)
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: After long longing, a king and queen celebrate the birth of their daughter Briar Rose, but they omit the thirteenth wise woman from the feast, provoking her to curse the child to die by a spindle…

stories.title: The Frog Prince
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: A spoiled princess accidentally drops her golden ball into a deep forest spring and secures the assistance of an ugly frog by promising to let him live with her as a companion.

stories.title: The Valiant Little Tailor
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: After killing seven flies in one stroke over a pot of jam, a humble tailor embroiders 'Seven at One Blow' on his belt and sets out to win his fortune, leading everyone to believe he vanquished seven…

stories.title: The Travelling Musicians (Bremen Town Musicians)
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: Facing abuse and execution after outliving their utility to their masters, an aging donkey, dog, cat, and rooster band together to seek livelihoods as musicians in the town of Bremen.

stories.title: The Twelve Dancing Princesses
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: A king discovers that his twelve daughters' shoes are mysteriously worn through every morning and decrees that whoever solves the secret within three days may marry one princess, while failures will…

stories.title: The Elves and the Shoemaker
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: An honest, destitute shoemaker cuts out his final piece of leather before bed, only to find it miraculously transformed into a flawless pair of shoes the next morning.

stories.title: The Golden Bird
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: When a golden bird steals golden apples from the royal garden, three princes set out sequentially to capture it, but only the youngest heeds the counsel of a talking fox.

stories.title: The Fisherman and His Wife
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: A poor fisherman catches an enchanted flounder prince who begs for his life, and the fisherman releases him back into the sea without asking for a reward.

stories.title: The Goose Girl
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: A royal maiden is sent abroad to wed a distant prince, carrying a magical horse named Falada and a handkerchief bearing three drops of her mother's protective blood.

stories.title: The Juniper Tree
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.place: Greifswald, Pomerania — Runge's Low German text
stories.teaser: A jealous stepmother beheads her young stepson with a heavy chest lid, frames her own daughter for the blow, and cooks the boy into a stew that his unwitting father eats.

stories.title: Jorinda and Jorindel
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: While walking near an enchanted castle in the deep forest, the maiden Jorinda is turned into a nightingale by an old sorceress, while her betrothed Jorindel is paralyzed and unable to move or speak.

stories.title: Old Sultan
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: When an aging farm dog named Old Sultan overhears his master planning to shoot him because he has lost his teeth and usefulness, he confides his plight to a sympathetic wolf in the woods.

stories.title: The Straw, the Coal, and the Bean
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: An old woman gathers straw, coal, and beans to cook a meal, but a single straw, a glowing ember of coal, and an escaped bean manage to slip away and decide to journey into the world together.

stories.title: The Dog and the Sparrow
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: A mistreated, starving sheepdog leaves his cruel master and befriends a clever sparrow, who leads him to town and procures meat and bread for him until the dog is satisfied.

stories.title: The Willow-Wren and the Bear
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: After a bear insults the young willow-wrens in their nest as disgraceful children, the father wren demands an apology and declares total war between all flying creatures and all four-footed beasts.

stories.title: The Cat and Mouse in Partnership
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: A cat and a mouse set up house together and buy a pot of fat for the winter, hiding it under the church altar for safekeeping.

stories.title: The Robber Bridegroom
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: A miller's daughter is betrothed against her instincts to a wealthy suitor and is forced to visit his remote mansion deep in the dark woods.

stories.title: Tom Thumb
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: A poor peasant couple is granted a son no bigger than a thumb, who grows up courageous and clever despite his miniature stature.

stories.title: Clever Gretel
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: Gretel, an indulgence-loving cook, prepares two chickens for her master and an invited guest, tasting the meat and wine repeatedly until she finishes both roasts completely.

stories.title: The Old Man and His Grandson
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: An elderly grandfather can no longer feed himself cleanly due to trembling hands and failing eyesight, so his frustrated son and daughter-in-law force him to sit in a corner behind the stove to eat…

stories.title: The Little Peasant
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: A poor peasant tricks his village into killing their cattle after claiming he sold a single calfskin for a fortune, prompting their murderous wrath.

stories.title: Frederick and Catherine
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: Catherine, the foolish wife of Frederick, creates a series of household disasters through disastrously literal thinking, including pouring out an entire beer cask while running after a dog and…

stories.title: Sweetheart Roland
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: To escape a wicked stepmother witch who plans to murder her, a maiden tricks the witch into killing her own favorite daughter instead, then flees into the wilderness with her beloved Roland.

stories.title: The Pink
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: A queen gives birth to a prince endowed with the magical power to have any wish granted, but a treacherous cook kidnaps the baby, frames the queen for infant murder, and hides the child in a distant…

stories.title: Clever Elsie
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: When a suitor named Hans comes seeking a clever bride, Elsie goes down to the cellar for beer and spots a pickaxe stuck in the wall above the barrel, weeping uncontrollably as she imagines it…

stories.title: The White Snake
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: A curious servant secretly tastes a morsel of the king's mysterious white snake dish, suddenly gaining the power to understand the speech of animals.

stories.title: The Wolf and the Seven Little Kids
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: Before venturing into the woods for food, an old goat warns her seven kids to beware the predatory wolf and recognize him by his rough voice and black feet.

stories.title: The Queen Bee
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: Two arrogant prince brothers waste their fortunes and prepare to destroy an anthill, kill ducks, and smoke out a beehive, but their simple-minded younger brother, nicknamed Simpleton, repeatedly…

stories.title: Mother Holle
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: An industrious stepdaughter is forced to spin by a well until her fingers bleed, and when she drops her shuttle into the water, her cruel stepmother orders her to jump down and retrieve it.

stories.title: The Story of the Youth Who Went Forth to Learn What Fear Was
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: A foolish young man who is incapable of shivering or feeling fear leaves home to learn how to shudder.

stories.title: King Grisly-Beard (King Thrushbeard)
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: A haughty princess mocks every noble suitor at a royal banquet, insulting an earnest king by nicknaming him 'Thrushbeard' due to his crooked chin.

stories.title: The Mouse, the Bird, and the Sausage
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: A mouse, a bird, and a sausage live together in harmonious prosperity by dividing their domestic labor according to their natural talents.

stories.title: The Miser in the Bush
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: A generous servant who receives only three farthings for years of work gives them away to a dwarf, who rewards him with a magic bird-shooting gun, a magic fiddle that compels everyone who hears it…

stories.title: Fundevogel
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: A forester rescues a baby boy named Fundevogel from an eagle's nest and raises him as a sibling alongside his daughter, Lena, forging an unbreakable bond between them.

stories.title: The Salad
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: A generous young huntsman receives a wishing-cloak and a gold-producing bird heart from an old woman, but an old witch and her beautiful daughter trick him into vomiting the heart and abandon him on…

stories.title: Brother and Sister
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: Fleeing their abusive stepmother, a brother and sister wander into a forest where the wicked woman has cursed all the springs; unable to resist his thirst, the brother drinks and is transformed into…

stories.title: Iron John (Eisenhans)
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: When a king's huntsmen drain a mysterious pool in the woods, they capture a wild, moss-covered man named Iron John and imprison him in a courtyard cage.

stories.title: The Three Snake-Leaves
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: A poor young soldier wins royal favor and marries the king's daughter, pledging an oath that should she die first, he will be buried alive in her vault.

stories.title: The Devil with the Three Golden Hairs
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: A poor boy born with a caul is prophesied to marry the king's daughter, prompting the wicked monarch to attempt to murder him in infancy and later send him with a death letter that is switched by…

stories.title: Doctor Knowall
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: A poor peasant named Crabb sells wood to a doctor, envies the physician's prosperity, and decides to become a doctor himself by buying an ABC book and putting up a sign reading 'Doctor Knowall'.

stories.title: Bearskin
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: A discharged soldier left destitute meets the Devil, who offers him boundless wealth on the condition that he neither wash, comb his hair, trim his nails, pray, nor take off a green coat and…

stories.title: Hans in Luck
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: After serving his master faithfully for seven years, Hans receives a lump of silver as big as his head as wages and sets off on foot to return to his mother.

stories.title: The Goose-Girl at the Well
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: An old woman living in a remote wilderness tends geese with an ugly, disguised maiden who performs backbreaking physical labor while crying tears of pearls.

stories.title: The Water of Life
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: When a king lies dying, his three sons seek the miraculous Water of Life, but the arrogant two elder sons are trapped in narrow mountain ravines after rudely insulting an encounter with a dwarf.

stories.title: The Two Brothers
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: Two identical twin brothers, raised by a huntsman after eating pieces of a magical golden bird, set out into the world accompanied by loyal wild beasts.

stories.title: The Four Clever Brothers
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: A poor father sends his four sons away to learn trades, and each returns as a master of a specialized skill: thief, astronomer, huntsman, and tailor.

stories.title: The Seven Ravens
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: A father accidentally curses his seven unruly sons into ravens after they fail to fetch baptismal water quickly for their sickly newborn sister.

stories.title: The Twelve Brothers
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: Twelve princes flee into the deep forest to escape execution by their father, who made twelve coffins to kill them if a daughter was born.

stories.title: The Singing Soaring Lark
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: A merchant seeks a singing, soaring lark for his youngest daughter, but must promise the beast guarding it—a ferocious lion—the first creature he meets at home, which happens to be his daughter.

stories.title: Fitcher's Bird
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: A sorcerer disguised as a beggar kidnaps three sisters one by one, testing each with an egg and a forbidden chamber in his secluded forest mansion.

stories.title: The Riddle
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: A traveling prince and his loyal servant encounter a witch whose poison kills the prince's horse; a raven eats the flesh and dies, and twelve robbers then eat the poisoned raven and perish.

stories.title: The Twelve Apostles
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: A desperately poor mother of twelve sons finds herself unable to feed them any longer and prays to God for deliverance, sending her children into the world under divine trust.

stories.title: The Star-Talers
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: An orphaned, destitute girl who owns nothing except the clothes on her back and a single piece of bread walks out into the open country, trusting entirely in God.

stories.title: The Sea-Hare
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: A haughty princess possesses a tower with twelve magical windows, allowing her to see everywhere on earth and execute any suitor who cannot hide from her gaze for a full day.

stories.title: The Master Thief
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: A destitute young man returns to his parents as a richly dressed master thief and reveals himself to his godfather, the local count.

stories.title: The Little Mermaid
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: The youngest mermaid princess falls deeply in love with a human prince she rescues from a shipwreck and longs for an immortal soul.

stories.title: The Ugly Duckling
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: A clumsy, unusually large bird hatches in a barnyard and is relentlessly harassed, bitten, and mocked by ducks, hens, and turkeys.

stories.title: The Snow Queen
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: Young playmates Kay and Gerda are separated when shards of a demonic hobgoblin mirror pierce Kay's heart and eyes, turning him cynical before he is swept away by the majestic Snow Queen to her…

stories.title: The Princess and the Pea
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: A prince travels across the world in search of a genuine princess to marry, but returns home disheartened because every candidate possessed flaws that left him doubting her authenticity.

stories.title: The Steadfast Tin Soldier
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: A one-legged tin soldier falls silently in love with a paper ballerina who balances on one foot before being knocked out a window by either the wind or a jealous goblin in a snuffbox.

stories.title: The Emperor's New Clothes
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: A vain emperor obsessed with magnificent clothing hires two swindlers who claim to weave fabric invisible to anyone stupid or incompetent in their office.

stories.title: Thumbelina
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: Born inside a blossoming flower to a childless woman, tiny Thumbelina is abducted from her walnut-shell cradle by an old toad who intends her as a bride for her muddy son.

stories.title: The Little Match Girl
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: On a freezing New Year's Eve, an impoverished little girl wanders barefoot through city streets, unable to sell any matches and terrified to return home to an abusive father.

stories.title: The Nightingale
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: The Emperor of China discovers that the most magnificent thing in his realm is the free song of a modest woodland nightingale, which moves him to tears when brought to court.

stories.title: The Tinderbox
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: A penniless soldier returning from war encounters a witch who offers him vast riches hidden inside a hollow tree guarded by three giant dogs, requiring only that he retrieve an old tinderbox.

stories.title: The Red Shoes
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: An impoverished orphan girl named Karen is adopted by an elderly benefactor and develops a sinful vanity centered upon a striking pair of red morocco shoes.

stories.title: The Wild Swans
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: Princess Elisa's eleven brothers are transformed into wild swans by an evil stepmother queen, while Elisa is cast out from the royal court.

stories.title: The Swineherd
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: A poor prince seeks the hand of the Emperor's daughter and sends her two rare treasures: an exquisite rose from a grave and a nightingale that sings divine melodies.

stories.title: Ole Lukøje
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: Ole Lukøje, the gentle dream-god who carries squirts of sweet milk and two umbrellas—one with pictures for good children and one plain for the naughty—visits a boy named Hjalmar over seven…

stories.title: The Marsh King's Daughter
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: An Egyptian princess flies north in swan disguise to gather healing lotus flowers from a Danish moor for her dying father, but she is pulled into the mire by the wicked Marsh King.

stories.title: The Garden of Paradise
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: A prince obsessed with finding the lost Garden of Eden journeys through an ancient forest until he reaches the Cave of the Winds, where Mother Wind introduces him to her sons.

stories.title: The Flying Trunk
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: A reckless merchant's son squanders his entire inheritance until he is left with nothing but a magical wooden trunk that can fly when its lock is pressed.

stories.title: The Shadow
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.place: Copenhagen — a hot southern city in the tale
stories.teaser: A scholarly man from cold northern climates settles in southern Europe, where he studies truth, beauty, and goodness; on an impulse, he bids his shadow cross the street to investigate a mysterious,…

stories.title: The Fir Tree
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: A young fir tree in a serene forest is perpetually dissatisfied with its small stature, ignoring the warmth of the sun and the song of birds while envying taller trees harvested for ship masts and…

stories.title: The Shepherdess and the Chimney Sweep
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: The lovers' escape reveals an overwhelming outside world, complicating the assumption that leaving confinement automatically produces confidence.

stories.title: The Snowman
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: A snowman's attraction to a stove links longing to the force that would destroy him; an embedded material explanation adds irony.

stories.title: The Storks
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: Children's taunts toward storks lead to a revenge-shaped explanation of how babies arrive; folkloric explanation carries unsettling punishment.

stories.title: The Goblin and the Huckster
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: The goblin is drawn to poetry's wonder but depends on the shopkeeper's material provision, leaving attraction and livelihood unresolved.

stories.title: Puss in Boots (Perrault)
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.place: Château d'Oiron — Marquis de Carabas legend
stories.teaser: The cat constructs his master's rank through gifts, staged appearances, and intimidation, showing reputation built through coordinated social evidence.

stories.title: Bluebeard (Perrault)
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.place: Tiffauges, Vendée — Gilles de Rais legend
stories.teaser: A prohibited room conceals murdered wives; the marked key turns discovery into evidence the captor can detect.

stories.title: Little Thumbling (Perrault)
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: The youngest child's observation and tactical substitutions preserve siblings whom stronger adults fail to protect.

stories.title: Ricky with the Tuft (Perrault)
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: Ricky and the princess negotiate valued qualities across unequal gifts, complicating whether attraction changes perception or the person themselves.

stories.title: Donkey Skin (Peau d'Âne) (Perrault)
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: An impossible marriage demand forces a princess to flee under a degrading disguise; survival precedes eventual recognition.

stories.title: The Fairies (Diamonds and Toads) (Perrault)
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: Speech produces jewels or repulsive creatures, making patterns of treatment visibly and materially consequential.

stories.title: Beauty and the Beast (Mme de Villeneuve / Mme de Beaumont)
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.attribution: Gabrielle-Suzanne de Villeneuve and Jeanne-Marie Leprince de Beaumont; distinct versions
stories.teaser: The Beaumont version develops reassessment through repeated encounters and a delayed return; Villeneuve's longer version supplies different family and fairy explanations.

stories.title: The Blue Bird (Mme d'Aulnoy)
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: A prince transformed into a bird maintains contact across confinement, but hostile interference makes that access dangerous.

stories.title: The White Cat (Mme d'Aulnoy)
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: A mysterious cat aids a prince's repeated tasks while concealing an enchanted identity and the conditions of release.

stories.title: Finette Cendron (Mme d'Aulnoy)
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: Finette's resourcefulness navigates abandonment, monstrous danger, and sibling rivalry; recognition follows repeated survival rather than a single rescue.

stories.title: Jack and the Beanstalk (English)
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: A small household exchange opens access to a giant's world; repeated trips increase both resources and pursuit risk.

stories.title: Jack the Giant Killer (English)
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: Jack's contests make apparent weakness advantageous through tricks that manipulate giants' assumptions about strength.

stories.title: Goldilocks and the Three Bears (Southey)
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.attribution: Robert Southey early account; later Goldilocks retellings
stories.teaser: Three sizes organize repeated intrusion and comparison; Southey's early version features an old woman rather than the later familiar girl.

stories.title: The Three Little Pigs (English)
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: Different building choices expose different resistance to the wolf; repeated attack makes preparation's consequences visible.

stories.title: Henny Penny (Chicken Little) (English)
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: A minor event becomes a catastrophic claim repeated through a group; some variants introduce a predator who exploits the panic.

stories.title: Childe Rowland (English)
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: A rescue into an enchanted realm depends on following prohibitions that distinguish the ordinary world from the dangerous one.

stories.title: Whittington and His Cat (English)
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: An apparently modest cat becomes valuable in another setting, linking mobility to a change in the meaning of a possession.

stories.title: The Golden Root (Basile – Pentamerone)
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: Basile's Golden Root belongs to the hidden-spouse and difficult-recovery pattern, where broken secrecy threatens an extraordinary relationship.

stories.title: Cenerentola (The Hearth Cat) (Basile – Pentamerone)
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: Basile's Zezolla participates in a stepmother's murder before suffering under a new household, complicating the innocent-victim Cinderella pattern.

stories.title: Sun, Moon, and Talia (Basile – Pentamerone)
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: Talia's unconscious assault and later threats are absorbed into a dynastic resolution, exposing the difference between a plot's reward and a character's consent.

stories.title: Penta the Maimed (Basile – Pentamerone)
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: Penta's resistance to an incestuous demand involves bodily injury, exile, and subsequent persecution, making autonomy costly within hostile power structures.

stories.title: Costanza / Costanzo (Straparola – The Facetious Nights)
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: Costanza's life as Costanzo uses male presentation to enter service and negotiate opportunities restricted by gendered expectations.

stories.title: Tam Lin (Child Ballad 39)
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.attribution: Traditional ballad; Francis James Child catalogue numbering
stories.teaser: Janet must hold Tam Lin through frightening transformations to reclaim him from the fairy company.

stories.title: The Elfin Knight (Child Ballad 2)
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.attribution: Traditional ballad; Francis James Child catalogue numbering
stories.teaser: Impossible demands are answered with equally impossible prerequisites, turning domination into a contest over the terms of obligation.

stories.title: Lady Isabel and the Elf-Knight (Child Ballad 4)
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.attribution: Traditional ballad; Francis James Child catalogue numbering
stories.teaser: A threatened woman redirects a murderous suitor's procedure and uses his expectations to reverse the immediate danger; versions differ.

stories.title: The Twa Sisters (Child Ballad 10)
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.attribution: Traditional ballad; Francis James Child catalogue numbering
stories.place: Stirling — the bonny mill-dams o' Binnorie
stories.teaser: A murdered sister's body becomes, or supplies, a musical instrument that reveals the crime in supernatural variants.

stories.title: Lord Randal (Child Ballad 12)
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.attribution: Traditional ballad; Francis James Child catalogue numbering
stories.teaser: Repeated questions gradually expose poisoning and intimate betrayal, allowing bodily symptoms to precede explicit accusation.

stories.title: Sir Patrick Spens (Child Ballad 58)
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.attribution: Traditional ballad; Francis James Child catalogue numbering
stories.teaser: An imposed voyage proceeds despite experienced warnings; ominous details make authority's refusal to listen central to the tragedy.

stories.title: The Wife of Usher's Well (Child Ballad 79)
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.attribution: Traditional ballad; Francis James Child catalogue numbering
stories.teaser: Dead sons return briefly to their mother, but the approaching dawn reasserts separation that desire cannot permanently overturn.

stories.title: Little Musgrave and Lady Barnard (Child Ballad 81)
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.attribution: Traditional ballad; Francis James Child catalogue numbering
stories.teaser: An affair across unequal social positions triggers violent retaliation, turning private desire into a crisis of status and possession.

stories.title: Barbara Allen (Child Ballad 84)
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.attribution: Traditional ballad; Francis James Child catalogue numbering
stories.teaser: A refusal becomes irreversible through death; subsequent grief and intertwined grave plants extend attachment beyond reconciliation.

stories.title: The Daemon Lover / House Carpenter (Child Ballad 243)
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.attribution: Traditional ballad; Francis James Child catalogue numbering
stories.teaser: A returning lover offers escape from domestic life but reveals a destructive supernatural destination; variants differ in moral emphasis.

stories.title: The Rime of the Ancient Mariner (Samuel Taylor Coleridge)
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: An arbitrary killing brings isolation and suffering; partial spiritual recovery does not erase the mariner's recurring need to narrate.

stories.title: The Erl-King (Der Erlkönig) (Johann Wolfgang von Goethe)
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: The child perceives a seductive supernatural pursuer while the father offers ordinary explanations; competing accounts persist through urgent motion.

stories.title: The Lady of Shalott (Alfred, Lord Tennyson)
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: A woman sees life through reflections under a prohibition; direct engagement breaks her protected artistic existence.

stories.title: The Eve of St. Agnes (John Keats)
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: A romantic encounter unfolds within a ritualized expectation of dreams and hostile family surroundings, complicating how desire and perception align.

stories.title: Childe Roland to the Dark Tower Came (Robert Browning)
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: The speaker advances through a hostile landscape toward an uncertain tower; persistence remains legible even when victory is withheld.

stories.title: The Highwayman (Alfred Noyes)
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: Bess's self-sacrificial warning saves her lover from an ambush, but incomplete information later draws him back toward death.

stories.title: Vasilisa the Beautiful
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.attribution: Slavic/Eastern European folk tradition; version unspecified
stories.teaser: A mother's doll aids Vasilisa through a hostile household and Baba Yaga's tasks, connecting inherited care to practical survival.

stories.title: The Death of Koschei the Deathless
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.attribution: Slavic/Eastern European folk tradition; version unspecified
stories.teaser: Koschei's death is hidden outside his body within nested containers, turning apparent invulnerability into a problem of locating dependencies.

stories.title: The Firebird and Tsarevich Ivan
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.attribution: Slavic/Eastern European folk tradition; version unspecified
stories.teaser: The Firebird quest links stolen wonders and dangerous promises; a powerful helper compensates for mistakes without removing their consequences.

stories.title: Sister Alenushka and Brother Ivanushka
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.attribution: Slavic/Eastern European folk tradition; version unspecified
stories.teaser: A brother's forbidden drink produces animal transformation while his sister's vulnerability attracts further danger.

stories.title: Father Frost (Morozko)
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.attribution: Slavic/Eastern European folk tradition; version unspecified
stories.teaser: Two girls encounter the same winter power under different dispositions; repetition makes treatment and response the basis of comparison.

stories.title: Go I Know Not Whither and Fetch I Know Not What
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.attribution: Slavic/Eastern European folk tradition; version unspecified
stories.teaser: A ruler weaponizes an unspecified impossible errand against a subordinate; help turns ambiguity into unexpected capability.

stories.title: The Frog Princess (Vasilisa the Wise)
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.attribution: Slavic/Eastern European folk tradition; version unspecified
stories.teaser: The frog bride's hidden capabilities challenge appearance-based judgment; destroying her skin too soon breaks the conditions of release.

stories.title: The Feather of Finist the Falcon
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.attribution: Slavic/Eastern European folk tradition; version unspecified
stories.teaser: A secretly visiting falcon lover is separated through hostile interference; the heroine's difficult search turns devotion into sustained action.

stories.title: The Sea King and Vasilisa the Wise
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.attribution: Slavic/Eastern European folk tradition; version unspecified
stories.teaser: The sea king's daughter solves impossible tasks and enables escape, while later forgetting threatens the bond that made survival possible.

stories.title: Twelve Months
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.attribution: Slavic/Eastern European folk tradition; version unspecified
stories.teaser: A girl sent for out-of-season goods receives aid from personified months; greedy imitation fails to reproduce the original relationship.

stories.title: The Tale of Tsar Saltan (Alexander Pushkin)
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: False messages separate a ruler from his wife and son; marvels and disguised visits rebuild the possibility of recognition.

stories.title: The Tale of the Golden Cockerel (Alexander Pushkin)
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: A king accepts an extraordinary warning device but resists its provider's claim, bringing political power into conflict with an earlier promise.

stories.title: The Tale of the Dead Princess and the Seven Knights (Alexander Pushkin)
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: A jealous queen pursues a displaced princess despite refuge among seven knights; repeated inquiry keeps the distant threat active.

stories.title: The Iliad (Homer)
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.teaser: Achilles' quarrel with Agamemnon removes a crucial fighter; Patroclus' death redirects wounded honor into devastating grief and revenge.

stories.title: The Odyssey (Homer)
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.teaser: Odysseus' return requires surviving strange hosts and concealing identity at home; recognition must distinguish loyalty from opportunism.

stories.title: Virgil's Aeneid
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.teaser: Aeneas' promised future demands departures and warfare; public destiny repeatedly conflicts with intimate attachment and mercy.

stories.title: The Argonautica (Apollonius of Rhodes)
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.teaser: Jason's expedition depends on diverse helpers and Medea's decisive assistance, making the prize inseparable from obligations created during acquisition.

stories.title: The Thebaid (Statius)
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.teaser: The brothers' struggle over Thebes draws allies into inherited hostility; reciprocal claims turn succession into collective catastrophe.

stories.title: The Achilleid (Statius)
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.teaser: The unfinished Achilleid follows Achilles' hidden upbringing on Scyros and exposure through martial inclinations; it does not complete his life story.

stories.title: The Works and Days (Hesiod)
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.teaser: Hesiod combines address to Perses, myths, and practical counsel to connect household conduct with justice and survival.

stories.title: The Theogony (Hesiod)
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.teaser: Divine generations establish order through birth, suppression, and overthrow; attempts to prevent succession help perpetuate conflict.

stories.title: Homeric Hymn to Demeter
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.attribution: Anonymous Homeric Hymn tradition; not assumed authored by Homer
stories.teaser: Demeter's loss becomes a crisis for gods and humans when withheld fertility makes private grief materially unavoidable.

stories.title: Homeric Hymn to Apollo
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.attribution: Anonymous Homeric Hymn tradition; not assumed authored by Homer
stories.teaser: Apollo's birth and establishment of sacred authority link divine identity to places, witnesses, and the creation of worship.

stories.title: Homeric Hymn to Hermes
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.attribution: Anonymous Homeric Hymn tradition; not assumed authored by Homer
stories.teaser: Hermes' theft and musical invention lead from conflict with Apollo to negotiated recognition within divine order.

stories.title: Homeric Hymn to Aphrodite
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.attribution: Anonymous Homeric Hymn tradition; not assumed authored by Homer
stories.teaser: Aphrodite experiences desire for a mortal, revealing vulnerability within the power she normally exercises over others.

stories.title: Prometheus Bound (Aeschylus)
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.teaser: Prometheus' physical confinement shifts conflict into endurance, testimony, and contested knowledge of the future; attribution to Aeschylus is debated.

stories.title: Agamemnon (Aeschylus)
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.teaser: Agamemnon's homecoming brings war's triumph into a household structured by prior sacrifice and revenge.

stories.title: Oedipus Rex (Sophocles)
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.teaser: Oedipus' attempt to save Thebes through investigation uncovers his own identity and involvement in the city's crisis.

stories.title: Oedipus at Colonus (Sophocles)
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.teaser: The aged Oedipus becomes politically valuable despite earlier exclusion, transforming a displaced person's destination into a contested source of power.

stories.title: Antigone (Sophocles)
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.teaser: Antigone's burial duty conflicts with Creon's decree; each side's absolutism narrows opportunities for correction.

stories.title: Medea (Euripides)
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.teaser: Medea's revenge against Jason destroys attachments she also values, making retaliation inseparable from catastrophic self-inflicted loss.

stories.title: The Bacchae (Euripides)
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.teaser: Pentheus' attempt to police Dionysian worship draws him into the spectacle he seeks to control, ending in fatal misrecognition.

stories.title: Hippolytus (Euripides)
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.teaser: Concealed desire, a damaging accusation, and a father's punitive response destroy Hippolytus before the account can be corrected.

stories.title: Creation and the Four Ages of Man
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.teaser: Ovid moves from creation to successive ages, compressing moral and material change into a patterned account of decline.

stories.title: Deucalion and Pyrrha (The Flood)
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.teaser: Flood survivors interpret a sacred instruction through an unexpected meaning, turning remnants of earth into a renewed human population.

stories.title: Apollo and Daphne
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.teaser: Daphne's escape from pursuit takes the form of bodily transformation, while Apollo claims an emblem from the changed body.

stories.title: Phaethon and the Sun Chariot
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.teaser: Phaethon demands control of the sun chariot as proof of parentage; the requested validation exceeds his ability and endangers the world.

stories.title: Echo and Narcissus
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.teaser: Echo can repeat but not initiate speech, while Narcissus mistakes his own reflection for an inaccessible other.

stories.title: Pyramus and Thisbe
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.teaser: A bloodied garment becomes false proof of death, and separated lovers act before the missing context can arrive.

stories.title: Perseus and Andromeda
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.teaser: Andromeda's exposure makes a political community's crisis fall on one person; Perseus' intervention links rescue to contested marriage and status.

stories.title: The Rape of Proserpina
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.teaser: Proserpina's abduction becomes a conflict among divine powers; a food-related condition helps produce a divided annual residence.

stories.title: Daedalus and Icarus
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.teaser: Wings enable escape but impose material limits; exhilaration and inattention turn liberation's device into a source of danger.

stories.title: Philemon and Baucis
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.teaser: An impoverished couple welcomes disguised gods whom others reject, making ordinary hospitality the test of a community's values.

stories.title: Orpheus and Eurydice
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.teaser: Orpheus wins a conditional return from death but loses it when he looks back before completing the exit.

stories.title: Pygmalion and Galatea
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.teaser: An artist's idealized sculpture becomes alive, turning a one-sided aesthetic attachment into the possibility of a relationship.

stories.title: Venus and Adonis
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.teaser: Venus' attachment cannot prevent Adonis' fatal encounter with a boar; divine desire meets limits of control.

stories.title: Atalanta and Hippomenes
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.teaser: Golden apples redirect Atalanta's attention during a marriage race, allowing another contestant's tactical aid to alter the outcome.

stories.title: Myrrha and Cinyras
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.teaser: Myrrha's concealed incestuous encounter ends in exposure and transformation; the narrative joins desire, mediation, and bodily aftermath.

stories.title: King Midas and the Golden Touch
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.teaser: Midas' gift converts nourishment and contact into unusable gold, exposing the difference between exchange value and conditions of life.

stories.title: The Death of Achilles
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.teaser: Ovid's account links Achilles' death to the survival of reputation and the struggle over his arms; later traditions add different bodily details.

stories.title: The Cipus Episode
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.teaser: Cipus learns a sign could bring kingship and chooses exclusion from the city rather than fulfill the threat to its liberty.

stories.title: Poetic Edda: Voluspo (The Wise-Woman's Prophecy)
stories.tradition: Norse Mythology: Poetic Edda & Prose Edda
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.attribution: Anonymous Poetic Edda materials; compilation and manuscript variation
stories.teaser: The seeress links origins, divine conflict, destruction, and renewal, making the present legible within a vast temporal frame.

stories.title: Poetic Edda: Hovamol (The Ballad of the High One)
stories.tradition: Norse Mythology: Poetic Edda & Prose Edda
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.attribution: Anonymous Poetic Edda materials; compilation and manuscript variation
stories.teaser: Havamal places practical conduct beside accounts of costly knowledge, holding everyday judgment and extraordinary self-sacrifice in one composite poem.

stories.title: Poetic Edda: Vafthruthnismol (Vafthruthnir's Sayings)
stories.tradition: Norse Mythology: Poetic Edda & Prose Edda
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.attribution: Anonymous Poetic Edda materials; compilation and manuscript variation
stories.teaser: Odin's wisdom contest becomes lethal when a final question reveals an asymmetry in who can know the answer.

stories.title: Poetic Edda: Grimnismol (Grimnir's Sayings)
stories.tradition: Norse Mythology: Poetic Edda & Prose Edda
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.attribution: Anonymous Poetic Edda materials; compilation and manuscript variation
stories.teaser: A disguised Odin is tortured while a younger figure offers care; revelation turns hospitality into a test of rulership.

stories.title: Poetic Edda: Skirnismol (Skirnir's Journey)
stories.tradition: Norse Mythology: Poetic Edda & Prose Edda
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.attribution: Anonymous Poetic Edda materials; compilation and manuscript variation
stories.teaser: Skirnir's mission pursues Gerdr through gifts and threats, exposing coercion within a formally successful marriage negotiation.

stories.title: Poetic Edda: Hymiskvitha (Hymir's Poem)
stories.tradition: Norse Mythology: Poetic Edda & Prose Edda
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.attribution: Anonymous Poetic Edda materials; compilation and manuscript variation
stories.teaser: Thor's quest for a giant brewing vessel links hospitality's practical needs to contests against forces beyond ordinary scale.

stories.title: Poetic Edda: Lokasenna (Loki's Wrangling)
stories.tradition: Norse Mythology: Poetic Edda & Prose Edda
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.attribution: Anonymous Poetic Edda materials; compilation and manuscript variation
stories.teaser: Loki's accusations disrupt a divine feast by exposing shame and contradiction; speech attacks the group's shared image of itself.

stories.title: Poetic Edda: Thrymskvitha (Thrym's Poem)
stories.tradition: Norse Mythology: Poetic Edda & Prose Edda
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.attribution: Anonymous Poetic Edda materials; compilation and manuscript variation
stories.teaser: Thor must perform an unexpected bridal role to recover his hammer, with Loki managing discrepancies that threaten the deception.

stories.title: Poetic Edda: Alvissmol (The Ballad of Alviss)
stories.tradition: Norse Mythology: Poetic Edda & Prose Edda
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.attribution: Anonymous Poetic Edda materials; compilation and manuscript variation
stories.teaser: Thor keeps Alviss answering questions until daylight defeats the suitor, making apparent intellectual competition a temporal trap.

stories.title: Poetic Edda: Baldrs Draumar (Baldr's Dreams)
stories.tradition: Norse Mythology: Poetic Edda & Prose Edda
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.attribution: Anonymous Poetic Edda materials; compilation and manuscript variation
stories.teaser: Odin seeks explanation for Baldr's ominous dreams, but information about loss does not provide easy power to prevent it.

stories.title: Poetic Edda: Rigsthula (The Lay of Rig)
stories.tradition: Norse Mythology: Poetic Edda & Prose Edda
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.attribution: Anonymous Poetic Edda materials; compilation and manuscript variation
stories.teaser: Rig's visits establish differentiated social lineages, presenting hierarchy as an origin narrative rather than a neutral observation.

stories.title: Poetic Edda: Volundarkvitha (The Lay of Völund)
stories.tradition: Norse Mythology: Poetic Edda & Prose Edda
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.attribution: Anonymous Poetic Edda materials; compilation and manuscript variation
stories.teaser: An imprisoned smith uses craft and concealment to enact devastating revenge on a ruler's household before escape.

stories.title: Poetic Edda: Helgakvitha Hundingsbana I & II
stories.tradition: Norse Mythology: Poetic Edda & Prose Edda
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.attribution: Anonymous Poetic Edda materials; compilation and manuscript variation
stories.teaser: The Helgi poems connect martial identity with love and death, using variant, overlapping materials rather than one seamless modern biography.

stories.title: Prose Edda: Prologue (Snorri Sturluson)
stories.tradition: Norse Mythology: Poetic Edda & Prose Edda
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.teaser: Snorri's prologue explains gods through human migration and ancestry, framing inherited myth for a different intellectual context.

stories.title: Prose Edda: Gylfaginning (The Beguiling of Gylfi)
stories.tradition: Norse Mythology: Poetic Edda & Prose Edda
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.teaser: A traveler's questioning organizes many divine stories within a deceptive encounter, making cosmology depend on a framed exchange.

stories.title: Prose Edda: Skáldskaparmál (The Language of Poetry)
stories.tradition: Norse Mythology: Poetic Edda & Prose Edda
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.teaser: Myths explain poetic circumlocutions, so understanding an image requires recalling a compressed narrative behind it.

stories.title: Prose Edda: Háttatal (Tally of Metres)
stories.tradition: Norse Mythology: Poetic Edda & Prose Edda
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.teaser: Hattatal demonstrates verse forms through praise poetry and commentary; it is not a single plot-driven tale.

stories.title: Völsunga Saga (Saga of the Volsungs)
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.teaser: Dragon treasure, broken promises, and dynastic marriages transmit injury across generations rather than ending with heroic acquisition.

stories.title: Ragnar Lodbrok Saga
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.teaser: Ragnar's desire for renown and his sons' rising fame connect personal expedition to dynastic rivalry and revenge.

stories.title: Saga of King Hrolf Kraki
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.place: Lejre, Zealand — hall of the Skjöldungs
stories.teaser: Hrolf's court concentrates extraordinary loyalty and prowess, yet betrayal and supernatural conflict expose the limits of an ideal retinue.

stories.title: Egil's Saga
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.attribution: Medieval Icelandic/Norse saga tradition; anonymous or compilation-specific
stories.teaser: Egil's poetry intervenes in conflicts where violence alone would fail, making artistic skill a practical resource within a dangerous reputation.

stories.title: Njál's Saga (Story of Burnt Njal)
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.attribution: Medieval Icelandic/Norse saga tradition; anonymous or compilation-specific
stories.teaser: Legal settlements repeatedly interact with honor and retaliation, showing how procedure can contain conflict only when participants accept its authority.

stories.title: Laxdæla Saga
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.attribution: Medieval Icelandic/Norse saga tradition; anonymous or compilation-specific
stories.teaser: Gudrun, Kjartan, and Bolli's entangled attachments turn marriage, pride, and loyalty into long-lived consequences.

stories.title: Gisli Sursson's Saga
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.attribution: Medieval Icelandic/Norse saga tradition; anonymous or compilation-specific
stories.teaser: Gisli's obligations entangle him in killing and outlawry, while concealment tests the people sustaining his survival.

stories.title: Eyrbyggja Saga
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.attribution: Medieval Icelandic/Norse saga tradition; anonymous or compilation-specific
stories.teaser: Disputes over land and authority coexist with hauntings, making the supernatural part of a community's contested memory.

stories.title: Saga of Erik the Red
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.attribution: Medieval Icelandic/Norse saga tradition; anonymous or compilation-specific
stories.teaser: The saga links Greenland and Vinland journeys with prophetic and religious episodes, reflecting a mediated account rather than a neutral travel log.

stories.title: Greenland Saga
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.attribution: Medieval Icelandic/Norse saga tradition; anonymous or compilation-specific
stories.teaser: Different Vinland ventures produce differing outcomes through leadership, trade, violence, and the limits of settlement.

stories.title: Grettir's Saga
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.attribution: Medieval Icelandic/Norse saga tradition; anonymous or compilation-specific
stories.teaser: Grettir's formidable strength cannot overcome the social and supernatural consequences of outlawry; survival grows increasingly isolated.

stories.title: Orkneyinga Saga
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.attribution: Medieval Icelandic/Norse saga tradition; anonymous or compilation-specific
stories.teaser: The earls' changing claims and alliances build a regional history through recurrent competition for rule.

stories.title: The Mabinogion: Pwyll Prince of Dyfed
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.attribution: Medieval Welsh narrative tradition; text-specific transmission
stories.teaser: Pwyll's exchange with Arawn makes honorable conduct in another ruler's position the basis of a lasting alliance.

stories.title: The Mabinogion: Branwen Daughter of Llyr
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.attribution: Medieval Welsh narrative tradition; text-specific transmission
stories.teaser: A marriage alliance is undermined by insult, reparation, abuse, and retaliatory war, making each attempted settlement inherit earlier harm.

stories.title: The Mabinogion: Manawydan Son of Llyr
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.attribution: Medieval Welsh narrative tradition; text-specific transmission
stories.teaser: Enchantment empties the land; Manawydan's patient labor and capture of a small culprit create leverage for restoration.

stories.title: The Mabinogion: Math Son of Mathonwy
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.attribution: Medieval Welsh narrative tradition; text-specific transmission
stories.teaser: Math's branch links magical punishment, manipulated birth conditions, and a woman made for a prescribed role who acts against that role.

stories.title: The Mabinogion: Dream of Rhonabwy
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.attribution: Medieval Welsh narrative tradition; text-specific transmission
stories.teaser: Rhonabwy's dream reframes heroic Arthurian grandeur through strange scale, delay, and retrospective distance.

stories.title: The Mabinogion: Culhwch and Olwen
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.attribution: Medieval Welsh narrative tradition; text-specific transmission
stories.teaser: Culhwch's marriage quest recruits Arthur's network to complete a chain of difficult tasks and an extraordinary hunt.

stories.title: The Mabinogion: The Tale of Taliesin
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.attribution: Medieval Welsh narrative tradition; text-specific transmission
stories.teaser: Gwion's acquisition of inspiration leads through transformation and rebirth into Taliesin; the tale's manuscript history differs from the Four Branches.

stories.title: Táin Bó Cúailnge (The Cattle Raid of Cooley)
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.attribution: Irish heroic or voyage tradition; version unspecified
stories.teaser: A cattle raid becomes a vast test of status and heroism; Cuchulainn's defense places personal loyalty against collective ambition.

stories.title: The Death of Cú Chulainn
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.attribution: Irish heroic or voyage tradition; version unspecified
stories.teaser: Traditions of Cuchulainn's death use converging obligations and prohibitions to close routes of escape while preserving a final heroic stance.

stories.title: The Pursuit of Diarmuid and Gráinne
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.attribution: Irish heroic or voyage tradition; version unspecified
stories.teaser: Diarmuid's bond to Fionn conflicts with Grainne's demands and their flight, making refuge inseparable from obligations left behind.

stories.title: The Voyage of Bran (Imram Brain)
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.attribution: Irish heroic or voyage tradition; version unspecified
stories.teaser: Bran's voyage reaches a different order of existence, while return reveals that time has passed differently at home.

stories.title: The Voyage of Saint Brendan
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.attribution: Irish heroic or voyage tradition; version unspecified
stories.teaser: Brendan's voyage organizes marvels through repeated observance and communal travel, making strange encounters part of spiritual orientation.

stories.title: The Children of Lir
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.attribution: Irish heroic or voyage tradition; version unspecified
stories.teaser: Children transformed into swans endure successive long periods of displacement, preserving familial attachment across a world that changes around them.

stories.title: The Exile of the Sons of Usnech (Deirdre of the Sorrows)
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.attribution: Irish heroic or voyage tradition; version unspecified
stories.teaser: Deirdre and the sons of Usnech return under promised protection that political betrayal destroys.

stories.title: The Sickbed of Cú Chulainn
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.attribution: Irish heroic or voyage tradition; version unspecified
stories.teaser: Cuchulainn's illness and encounter with Fand bring an extraordinary attachment into conflict with existing bonds and their repair.

stories.title: The Colloquy of the Old Men (Acallam na Senórach)
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.attribution: Irish heroic or voyage tradition; version unspecified
stories.teaser: Surviving warriors recount older adventures to Patrick, linking place names and remembered events while negotiating different religious worlds.

stories.title: The Kalevala: Runo 1 (Creation of the World & Birth of Väinämöinen)
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.attribution: Elias Lonnrot, Kalevala compiler; drawing on oral poetry
stories.teaser: The opening runo links a primordial water world, the air maiden, and cosmic formation, placing human song within a larger origin.

stories.title: The Kalevala: Runo 3 (Väinämöinen and Joukahainen)
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.attribution: Elias Lonnrot, Kalevala compiler; drawing on oral poetry
stories.teaser: Joukahainen's competitive boasting meets Vainamoinen's superior song, and an escape bargain transfers the cost to his sister Aino.

stories.title: The Kalevala: Runo 10 (Forging of the Sampo by Ilmarinen)
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.attribution: Elias Lonnrot, Kalevala compiler; drawing on oral poetry
stories.teaser: Ilmarinen's forging of the Sampo ties exceptional craftsmanship to promises, political possession, and later competition over prosperity.

stories.title: The Kalevala: Runo 14–15 (Lemminkäinen's Death & Resurrection)
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.attribution: Elias Lonnrot, Kalevala compiler; drawing on oral poetry
stories.teaser: Lemminkainen's death is answered by his mother's search and recovery of scattered remains, making care a practical restoration task.

stories.title: The Kalevala: Runo 31–36 (The Tragedy of Kullervo)
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.attribution: Elias Lonnrot, Kalevala compiler; drawing on oral poetry
stories.teaser: Kullervo's dispossession and mistreatment precede destructive revenge and catastrophic recognition, linking damage suffered to damage inflicted.

stories.title: The Kalevala: Runo 42–43 (The Theft and Destruction of the Sampo)
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.attribution: Elias Lonnrot, Kalevala compiler; drawing on oral poetry
stories.teaser: The expedition to recover the Sampo ends in conflict and fragmentation, making prosperity's distribution inseparable from its destruction.

stories.title: Kalevipoeg (Estonian National Epic by Friedrich Reinhold Kreutzwald)
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.teaser: Kalevipoeg's extraordinary strength and kingship coexist with errors, a consequential sword, and an ending that limits uncomplicated national triumph.

stories.title: Lāčplēsis (The Bear-Slayer) (Latvian Epic by Andrejs Pumpurs)
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.teaser: Lacplesis embodies extraordinary power and national struggle, but a distinctive bodily vulnerability makes the final conflict possible.

stories.title: Shahnameh (Book of Kings): The Legend of Zal and Simurgh (Ferdowsi)
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.teaser: Zal's unusual appearance prompts abandonment, while the Simurgh's care produces capacities his birth community failed to recognize.

stories.title: Shahnameh: The Tragedy of Rostam and Sohrab (Ferdowsi)
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.teaser: Rostam and Sohrab fight without recognizing their relationship; withheld and incomplete identity information makes prowess catastrophic.

stories.title: Shahnameh: The Story of Sevavush (Ferdowsi)
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.teaser: Siyavush survives an accusation but remains vulnerable to political betrayal abroad, separating vindication from actual protection.

stories.title: Shahnameh: Rostam's Seven Labors (Haft Khan) (Ferdowsi)
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.teaser: Rostam's seven labors alternate kinds of danger on a rescue journey, testing more than one form of heroic competence.

stories.title: Layla and Majnun (Nizami Ganjavi)
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.place: Najd, Arabia — Nizami of Ganja's setting
stories.teaser: Majnun's devotion conflicts with social arrangements and ordinary participation, turning separation into a sustained identity rather than a brief obstacle.

stories.title: Khosrow and Shirin (Nizami Ganjavi)
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.teaser: Royal desire, Shirin's conditions, and Farhad's labor place love in unequal relations to political authority and practical effort.

stories.title: Saman-nameh (Attributed to Khaju Kermani)
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.attribution: Sam-nama candidate; attributed to Khwaju Kermani, disputed
stories.teaser: The probable Sam-nama match follows Sam's heroic struggles toward reunion with Princess Paridokht, linking martial adventure with romantic desire; the work's attribution is disputed.

stories.title: The Conference of the Birds (Mantiq al-Tayr) (Farid ud-Din Attar)
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.teaser: The birds' search for the Simurgh culminates in recognition that transforms the distinction between seekers and sought.

stories.title: Valmiki Ramayana: Bala Kanda (The Boyhood of Rama)
stories.section: Asian & Eastern Sacred Epics, Scriptures & Narrative Poems
stories.attribution: Ramayana traditionally attributed to Valmiki; textual variation
stories.teaser: Rama's early training and marriage test connect education, extraordinary capacity, and public recognition before the larger crisis.

stories.title: Valmiki Ramayana: Ayodhya Kanda (The Exile of Rama)
stories.section: Asian & Eastern Sacred Epics, Scriptures & Narrative Poems
stories.attribution: Ramayana traditionally attributed to Valmiki; textual variation
stories.teaser: A prior royal promise redirects succession into Rama's exile, testing obligations among ruler, spouses, brothers, and subjects.

stories.title: Valmiki Ramayana: Aranya Kanda (The Forest Life & Abduction of Sita)
stories.section: Asian & Eastern Sacred Epics, Scriptures & Narrative Poems
stories.attribution: Ramayana traditionally attributed to Valmiki; textual variation
stories.teaser: Forest exile becomes a separation crisis through an enticing diversion and Ravana's abduction of Sita; details vary by telling.

stories.title: Valmiki Ramayana: Kishkindha Kanda (Alliance with Sugriva and Hanuman)
stories.section: Asian & Eastern Sacred Epics, Scriptures & Narrative Poems
stories.attribution: Ramayana traditionally attributed to Valmiki; textual variation
stories.teaser: Rama's search becomes linked to Sugriva's struggle with Vali, making assistance depend on another community's contested leadership.

stories.title: Valmiki Ramayana: Sundara Kanda (Hanuman's Leap to Lanka)
stories.section: Asian & Eastern Sacred Epics, Scriptures & Narrative Poems
stories.attribution: Ramayana traditionally attributed to Valmiki; textual variation
stories.teaser: Hanuman's crossing, search, meeting with Sita, and return make information and reassurance central achievements before military victory.

stories.title: Valmiki Ramayana: Yuddha Kanda (The Great Battle of Lanka)
stories.section: Asian & Eastern Sacred Epics, Scriptures & Narrative Poems
stories.attribution: Ramayana traditionally attributed to Valmiki; textual variation
stories.teaser: The Lanka campaign coordinates allies and extraordinary weapons while making rescue, kingship, and the treatment of Sita contested concerns.

stories.title: Valmiki Ramayana: Uttara Kanda (The Final Trial and Ascension)
stories.section: Asian & Eastern Sacred Epics, Scriptures & Narrative Poems
stories.attribution: Ramayana traditionally attributed to Valmiki; textual variation
stories.teaser: The Uttara Kanda revisits kingship, public suspicion, Sita's exclusion, and the next generation; its textual status and interpretation vary.

stories.title: Dutt's Condensed Ramayana & Mahabharata Epics
stories.section: Asian & Eastern Sacred Epics, Scriptures & Narrative Poems
stories.teaser: Dutt's paired adaptations condense two epics, making selection and emphasis part of the storytelling rather than a replacement for every source episode.

stories.title: Mahabharata: Adi Parva (The Book of Beginnings & Shakuntala)
stories.section: Asian & Eastern Sacred Epics, Scriptures & Narrative Poems
stories.attribution: Mahabharata traditionally attributed to Vyasa; layered textual tradition
stories.teaser: The Adi Parva establishes lineages, births, rivalries, and embedded stories that give later succession conflicts their stakes.

stories.title: Mahabharata: Sabha Parva (The Book of the Assembly Hall & Dice Game)
stories.section: Asian & Eastern Sacred Epics, Scriptures & Narrative Poems
stories.attribution: Mahabharata traditionally attributed to Vyasa; layered textual tradition
stories.teaser: The dice game turns accepted court procedure into dispossession and public violation, exposing failures of authority within an apparently lawful setting.

stories.title: Mahabharata: Vana Parva (Forest Exile, Nala and Damayanti, Savitri and Satyavan)
stories.section: Asian & Eastern Sacred Epics, Scriptures & Narrative Poems
stories.attribution: Mahabharata traditionally attributed to Vyasa; layered textual tradition
stories.teaser: The forest book places the exiled Pandavas beside narratives such as Nala and Savitri, using other lives to examine their predicament.

stories.title: Mahabharata: Virata Parva (Incognito Year at Virata's Court)
stories.section: Asian & Eastern Sacred Epics, Scriptures & Narrative Poems
stories.attribution: Mahabharata traditionally attributed to Vyasa; layered textual tradition
stories.teaser: The Pandavas' concealed year requires capable people to limit public displays until a time-bound condition is satisfied.

stories.title: Mahabharata: Udyoga Parva (War Council & Peace Negotiations)
stories.section: Asian & Eastern Sacred Epics, Scriptures & Narrative Poems
stories.attribution: Mahabharata traditionally attributed to Vyasa; layered textual tradition
stories.teaser: Diplomatic efforts and competing demands establish what might avert war and why the available settlement fails.

stories.title: Mahabharata: Bhishma Parva (Bhishma's Command & The Bhagavad Gita)
stories.section: Asian & Eastern Sacred Epics, Scriptures & Narrative Poems
stories.attribution: Mahabharata traditionally attributed to Vyasa; layered textual tradition
stories.teaser: Arjuna's battlefield hesitation opens the Gita's inquiry into action and obligation within an imminent war, not an abstract motivational pause.

stories.title: Mahabharata: Drona Parva (Fall of Abhimanyu & Death of Drona)
stories.section: Asian & Eastern Sacred Epics, Scriptures & Narrative Poems
stories.attribution: Mahabharata traditionally attributed to Vyasa; layered textual tradition
stories.teaser: Abhimanyu's death and the effort to defeat Drona expose how tactical advantage tests commitments to fair conduct.

stories.title: Mahabharata: Karna Parva (Karna's Leadership & Duel with Arjuna)
stories.section: Asian & Eastern Sacred Epics, Scriptures & Narrative Poems
stories.attribution: Mahabharata traditionally attributed to Vyasa; layered textual tradition
stories.teaser: Karna's final combat carries accumulated loyalties, revelations, curses, and disadvantages into a duel whose meaning exceeds skill alone.

stories.title: Mahabharata: Shalya Parva (Duryodhana's Last Stand)
stories.section: Asian & Eastern Sacred Epics, Scriptures & Narrative Poems
stories.attribution: Mahabharata traditionally attributed to Vyasa; layered textual tradition
stories.teaser: Duryodhana's last stand and the decisive mace duel leave the winners' methods open to dispute even as military resistance collapses.

stories.title: Mahabharata: Sauptika Parva (Ashwatthama's Night Attack)
stories.section: Asian & Eastern Sacred Epics, Scriptures & Narrative Poems
stories.attribution: Mahabharata traditionally attributed to Vyasa; layered textual tradition
stories.teaser: Ashwatthama's night attack destroys lives after the main battle appears settled, showing revenge's capacity to outlive formal victory.

stories.title: Mahabharata: Stri Parva (Lament of Queens & Gandhari's Curse)
stories.section: Asian & Eastern Sacred Epics, Scriptures & Narrative Poems
stories.attribution: Mahabharata traditionally attributed to Vyasa; layered textual tradition
stories.place: Kurukshetra — the field of the dead
stories.teaser: The lamenting women and Gandhari's response shift attention from battlefield achievement to the families and futures it destroys.

stories.title: Mahabharata: Shanti Parva (Bhishma's Discourse on Dharma and Governance)
stories.section: Asian & Eastern Sacred Epics, Scriptures & Narrative Poems
stories.attribution: Mahabharata traditionally attributed to Vyasa; layered textual tradition
stories.teaser: Bhishma's teachings address the difficulty of ruling after destruction, turning succession into a burden of judgment rather than a final reward.

stories.title: Mahabharata: Mahaprasthanika Parva (Ascent of the Pandavas to the Himalayas)
stories.section: Asian & Eastern Sacred Epics, Scriptures & Narrative Poems
stories.attribution: Mahabharata traditionally attributed to Vyasa; layered textual tradition
stories.teaser: The Pandavas' last journey strips away companions and worldly position, testing how attachment and judgment operate near death.

stories.title: Bhagavata Purana: Rasa Lila (The Divine Dance of Krishna)
stories.section: Asian & Eastern Sacred Epics, Scriptures & Narrative Poems
stories.teaser: The Rasa Lila presents Krishna's relation to the gopis within devotional theology; union and absence carry meanings beyond ordinary courtship.
