stories.title: Devi Mahatmyam ( दुर्गासप्तशती - Slaying of Mahishasura & Sumbha-Nisumbha)
stories.section: Asian & Eastern Sacred Epics, Scriptures & Narrative Poems
stories.attribution: Devi Mahatmyam, embedded in the Markandeya Purana
stories.teaser: The Devi's battles present divine feminine power confronting threats that other powers cannot overcome; the episodes differ in adversaries and tactics.

stories.title: Gita Govinda (Jayadeva)
stories.section: Asian & Eastern Sacred Epics, Scriptures & Narrative Poems
stories.teaser: Jayadeva's poem develops Radha and Krishna's estrangement and reunion through songs, mediation, and devotional-erotic imagery.

stories.title: The Turtle Who Couldn't Stop Talking (Kacchapa Jataka)
stories.section: Asian & Eastern Sacred Epics, Scriptures & Narrative Poems
stories.attribution: Buddhist Jataka traditions; title and numbering require text-specific attribution
stories.teaser: The turtle's transport works only while he keeps his mouth closed; reacting to taunts breaks the mechanism supporting him.

stories.title: Kapota-Jātaka (The Pigeon and the Greedy Crow)
stories.section: Asian & Eastern Sacred Epics, Scriptures & Narrative Poems
stories.attribution: Buddhist Jataka traditions; title and numbering require text-specific attribution
stories.teaser: The crow's appetite drives deception and entry into a kitchen, while the pigeon's restraint supplies a contrasting response to temptation.

stories.title: Takka-Jātaka (The Ascetic and the Woman)
stories.section: Asian & Eastern Sacred Epics, Scriptures & Narrative Poems
stories.attribution: Buddhist Jataka traditions; title and numbering require text-specific attribution
stories.teaser: The Takka tale depicts an ascetic's entanglement with a woman and subsequent betrayal within a historically misogynistic cautionary frame.

stories.title: Kuṇāla-Jātaka (Dispute Over Irrigation Water)
stories.section: Asian & Eastern Sacred Epics, Scriptures & Narrative Poems
stories.attribution: Buddhist Jataka traditions; title and numbering require text-specific attribution
stories.teaser: The irrigation quarrel occurs in the framing material associated with Kunala Jataka; the full work contains many other stories and themes.

stories.title: Godha-Jātaka (The False Ascetic and the Lizard - Jataka 325/326)
stories.section: Asian & Eastern Sacred Epics, Scriptures & Narrative Poems
stories.attribution: Buddhist Jataka traditions; title and numbering require text-specific attribution
stories.teaser: In Godha Jataka 325, an ascetic's appetite turns a respectful relationship with a lizard into attempted predation; 326 is a different tale.

stories.title: Mahakapi Jataka (The Monkey King's Sacrifice)
stories.section: Asian & Eastern Sacred Epics, Scriptures & Narrative Poems
stories.attribution: Buddhist Jataka traditions; title and numbering require text-specific attribution
stories.teaser: The monkey king uses his body to enable the troop's escape, making leadership a concrete assumption of others' risk.

stories.title: Vessantara Jataka (The Great Charity of Prince Vessantara)
stories.section: Asian & Eastern Sacred Epics, Scriptures & Narrative Poems
stories.attribution: Buddhist Jataka traditions; title and numbering require text-specific attribution
stories.teaser: Vessantara's radical giving extends into family relationships, making generosity and obligations to dependents difficult to separate.

stories.title: Banyan Deer Jataka (Self-Sacrifice for the Herd)
stories.section: Asian & Eastern Sacred Epics, Scriptures & Narrative Poems
stories.attribution: Buddhist Jataka traditions; title and numbering require text-specific attribution
stories.teaser: The deer king offers himself in place of another, bringing a ruler's hunting arrangement into contact with an individual act of compassion.

stories.title: The Lotus Sutra: Parable of the Burning House (Chapter 3)
stories.section: Asian & Eastern Sacred Epics, Scriptures & Narrative Poems
stories.teaser: Children absorbed in play must be drawn out of a burning house; promised vehicles make urgent instruction intelligible to them.

stories.title: The Lotus Sutra: Parable of the Poor Son (Chapter 4)
stories.section: Asian & Eastern Sacred Epics, Scriptures & Narrative Poems
stories.teaser: An estranged son is gradually prepared to recognize an inheritance he initially cannot imagine accepting.

stories.title: The Lotus Sutra: Parable of the Medicinal Herbs (Chapter 5)
stories.section: Asian & Eastern Sacred Epics, Scriptures & Narrative Poems
stories.teaser: Rain nourishes different plants according to their capacities, using ecological comparison to explain differentiated reception of teaching.

stories.title: The Lotus Sutra: Parable of the Conjured City (Chapter 7)
stories.section: Asian & Eastern Sacred Epics, Scriptures & Narrative Poems
stories.teaser: A conjured city provides exhausted travelers a temporary resting point on a longer journey; the refuge is useful without being the destination.

stories.title: The Lotus Sutra: Parable of the Pearl in the Garment (Chapter 8)
stories.section: Asian & Eastern Sacred Epics, Scriptures & Narrative Poems
stories.teaser: A person lives in deprivation without knowing a jewel is already sewn into their garment, making recognition rather than acquisition decisive.

stories.title: Buddhacarita (Acts of the Buddha) (Aśvaghoṣa)
stories.section: Asian & Eastern Sacred Epics, Scriptures & Narrative Poems
stories.teaser: The prince's encounter with suffering changes what royal security can mean, leading to renunciation and a search for liberation.

stories.title: The Epic of Gilgamesh (Tablets I–XII)
stories.section: Asian & Eastern Sacred Epics, Scriptures & Narrative Poems
stories.attribution: Ancient Near Eastern literary tradition; text-specific versions
stories.teaser: Enkidu's death redirects Gilgamesh from heroic achievement toward mortality; the failed search for lasting life reshapes attention to human limits.

stories.title: Enuma Elish (Babylonian Epic of Creation)
stories.section: Asian & Eastern Sacred Epics, Scriptures & Narrative Poems
stories.attribution: Ancient Near Eastern literary tradition; text-specific versions
stories.teaser: Marduk's victory over Tiamat establishes cosmic arrangements and political-theological primacy, tying creation to a hierarchy justified through battle.

stories.title: The Descent of Inanna to the Underworld
stories.section: Asian & Eastern Sacred Epics, Scriptures & Narrative Poems
stories.attribution: Ancient Near Eastern literary tradition; text-specific versions
stories.teaser: Inanna loses regalia at successive gates, making descent a structured stripping of status before death and negotiated return.

stories.title: Atrahasis Epic (The Mesopotamian Flood Narrative)
stories.section: Asian & Eastern Sacred Epics, Scriptures & Narrative Poems
stories.attribution: Ancient Near Eastern literary tradition; text-specific versions
stories.teaser: Divine attempts to manage human disturbance escalate toward flood, followed by arrangements limiting future population and vulnerability.

stories.title: The Legend of Aqhat
stories.section: Asian & Eastern Sacred Epics, Scriptures & Narrative Poems
stories.attribution: Ancient Near Eastern literary tradition; text-specific versions
stories.teaser: Aqhat's refusal of a goddess's demand for his bow leads to lethal consequences and a surviving family's response; the text is fragmentary.

stories.title: The Baal Cycle (Tales of Yam, Mot, and Baal)
stories.section: Asian & Eastern Sacred Epics, Scriptures & Narrative Poems
stories.attribution: Ancient Near Eastern literary tradition; text-specific versions
stories.teaser: Baal's struggles with Yam and Mot connect kingship to sea, death, and renewed life rather than a single permanent conquest.

stories.title: The Myth of Adapa and the South Wind
stories.section: Asian & Eastern Sacred Epics, Scriptures & Narrative Poems
stories.attribution: Ancient Near Eastern literary tradition; text-specific versions
stories.teaser: Adapa follows advice against accepting food and drink in heaven, yet the offered gift carries a possibility the advice does not transparently secure.

stories.title: The Tale of the Doomed Prince (Egyptian)
stories.section: Asian & Eastern Sacred Epics, Scriptures & Narrative Poems
stories.attribution: Ancient Near Eastern literary tradition; text-specific versions
stories.teaser: A prince is warned of three forms of death; surviving individual threats does not settle the prophecy, and the preserved ending is incomplete.

stories.title: The Tale of the Two Brothers (Egyptian)
stories.section: Asian & Eastern Sacred Epics, Scriptures & Narrative Poems
stories.attribution: Ancient Near Eastern literary tradition; text-specific versions
stories.teaser: The Egyptian brothers' story moves from false accusation through separation and repeated transformations, carrying betrayal across changing identities.

stories.title: The Shipwrecked Sailor (Egyptian)
stories.section: Asian & Eastern Sacred Epics, Scriptures & Narrative Poems
stories.attribution: Ancient Near Eastern literary tradition; text-specific versions
stories.teaser: A sailor recounts survival on a marvelous island to frame present anxiety, using an embedded voyage to offer reassurance after failure.

stories.title: Journey to the West (Xi You Ji - Sun Wukong / Monkey King)
stories.tradition: Chinese Classic Narrative Epics & Mythic Lore
stories.section: Asian & Eastern Sacred Epics, Scriptures & Narrative Poems
stories.attribution: Journey to the West, traditionally attributed to Wu Cheng’en
stories.teaser: The pilgrimage's companions bring distinct strengths and appetites to recurring ordeals, turning travel into sustained discipline rather than simple movement.

stories.title: Investiture of the Gods (Fengshen Yanyi)
stories.tradition: Chinese Classic Narrative Epics & Mythic Lore
stories.section: Asian & Eastern Sacred Epics, Scriptures & Narrative Poems
stories.attribution: Investiture of the Gods, traditionally attributed to Xu Zhonglin
stories.teaser: Dynastic war and divine participation converge in the allocation of celestial offices, giving casualties roles within a larger order.

stories.title: The Ballad of Mulan (Mulan Ci)
stories.tradition: Chinese Classic Narrative Epics & Mythic Lore
stories.section: Asian & Eastern Sacred Epics, Scriptures & Narrative Poems
stories.teaser: Mulan takes her father's place in military service; the ballad foregrounds family duty and delayed recognition rather than later screen adaptations' romances.

stories.title: Legend of the White Snake (Baishe Zhuan)
stories.tradition: Chinese Classic Narrative Epics & Mythic Lore
stories.section: Asian & Eastern Sacred Epics, Scriptures & Narrative Poems
stories.teaser: The white snake's human life and marriage encounter religious intervention and fear of nonhuman identity; versions distribute sympathy differently.

stories.title: Classic of Mountains and Seas (Shan Hai Jing)
stories.tradition: Chinese Classic Narrative Epics & Mythic Lore
stories.section: Asian & Eastern Sacred Epics, Scriptures & Narrative Poems
stories.teaser: The Classic organizes mountains, waters, beings, and distant peoples in a heterogeneous geographic-mythic compendium, not one continuous adventure.

stories.title: The Cowherd and the Weaver Girl (Niu Lang Zhi Nu)
stories.tradition: Chinese Classic Narrative Epics & Mythic Lore
stories.section: Asian & Eastern Sacred Epics, Scriptures & Narrative Poems
stories.teaser: The lovers' separation across the sky and limited reunion give longing a recurring temporal structure.

stories.title: Nuwa Mends the Heavens
stories.tradition: Chinese Classic Narrative Epics & Mythic Lore
stories.section: Asian & Eastern Sacred Epics, Scriptures & Narrative Poems
stories.teaser: Nuwa repairs a damaged world through extraordinary materials and labor, making creation continue as maintenance after catastrophe.

stories.title: Hou Yi Shoots the Nine Suns
